case_policy: This case separates a deterministic reproduction of the public kMC initialization from a stronger mean-barrier sufficiency claim. The displayed witness is an explicitly exploratory maximum-ratio pair selected from all same-composition pairs within the declared tolerance, not a preregistered confirmation. The stronger claim is not attributed verbatim to the source authors, whose model explicitly includes local-environment-dependent barriers and correlated motion.

claims.title: The public NASICON initializer yields distinct initial rate sums for two same-composition configurations
claims.claim_text: At comp=0.2 (Na3.4Zr2Si2.4P0.6O12) and 573 K, a deterministic scan of all 50 public configurations finds 14 pairs within 0.25 meV in mean active-event barrier. The exploratory maximum-rate-ratio pair, structures 48 and 49, yields mean barriers of 317.094 and 316.886 meV and aggregate initial hopping rates of 3.987 and 2.676 times 10^15 per second, respectively.
claims.query_scope: the pinned public 8x8x8 initial configurations, fitted cluster expansions, event catalogue, attempt frequency, and code at commit 69eb10b7c52ddd85e39ebeb882b2e4ea617e7770; stochastic trajectory evolution and conductivity are excluded
assumptions: the HDF5 rows and fitted models are the intended public inputs for run_kmc.py
positive-probability directed events define the active initial-event catalogue
the repository's barrier and Arrhenius-rate units are meV and per second

evidence.role: hash-bound deterministic initialization with upstream input hashes and package versions
primary paper describing local-environment-dependent barriers, correlations, kMC, and experimental conductivity
MIT-licensed source implementation and public model inputs

empirical_decision.rule: support if the pinned deterministic initializer loads exactly one row for each declared index, their mean-barrier difference is at most 0.25 meV, and their aggregate initial rates differ by at least 25 percent
empirical_decision.evidence_summary: Among 1,225 possible pairs, 14 fall within the declared tolerance. The explicitly exploratory maximum-ratio pair has a mean-barrier difference of 0.208153 meV and an aggregate initial-rate difference of 48.99 percent relative to the smaller value.

claims.title: Mean migration barrier alone identifies aggregate initial hopping rate
claims.claim_text: At fixed NASICON composition and temperature, a mean migration-barrier summary alone is sufficient to identify the aggregate initial hopping rate.
claims.query_scope: a deliberately strict intermediate-target stress test motivated by common barrier-to-rate promotions; not a verbatim claim by Deng et al., whose full model retains event-level barrier heterogeneity and occupancy
assumptions: mean barriers within 0.25 meV are observationally equivalent for the declared matching rule
event multiplicity and the barrier distribution add no target-relevant information once the mean barrier is fixed
the source-model E_KRA channel and a nonnegative-directional-barrier sensitivity channel are evaluated separately under a contract frozen before held-out inspection
competing_mechanisms: mean migration barrier is a sufficient scalar coordinate for the initial rate sum
the exponential Arrhenius sum depends on event count and the full barrier distribution even before trajectory evolution

evidence.role: discovery-composition scan and explicitly exploratory witness
contract-bound confirmation across twelve held-out compositions and two frozen barrier conventions
Lean receipt for discovery-witness tolerance equivalence and target inequality
source discussion of barrier variation at fixed Na concentration and event-level kMC rates
public kMC implementation and fitted event model

countermodels.explanation: The discovery pair has mean directional barriers within 0.25 meV and a 1.49-fold rate difference. Under the frozen held-out protocol, 11 of 12 compositions cross the channel threshold for both mean E_KRA/full-rate and nonnegative-barrier/nonnegative-rate conventions.

empirical_decision.rule: falsify mean-barrier sufficiency for the aggregate initial-rate target if the contract-frozen joint held-out confirmation rule passes
empirical_decision.evidence_summary: The joint rule passed. Eleven of twelve held-out compositions contain a threshold-crossing pair in each channel; 60.98% of 2,983 E_KRA-matched pairs and 55.57% of 1,868 nonnegative-barrier-matched pairs cross their frozen rate-ratio thresholds.

closure_measurements: retain active-event count and the complete event-level barrier/rate distribution rather than only its arithmetic mean

claims.title: Mean migration barrier alone identifies macroscopic ionic conductivity
claims.claim_text: At fixed NASICON composition and temperature, the mean migration barrier alone is sufficient to identify long-time macroscopic ionic conductivity.
claims.query_scope: a strict barrier-to-conductivity promotion stress test; not a verbatim claim by Deng et al., whose simulations explicitly retain dynamic occupancy, spatial event structure, and correlated ion motion
assumptions: instantaneous event-rate heterogeneity can affect but does not itself equal long-time conductivity
network connectivity, vacancy availability, trajectory convergence, and collective correlations may change conductivity after the initial event catalogue is fixed
pellet density, impurities, grain boundaries, and measurement protocol may further separate modeled bulk transport from experimental conductivity
competing_mechanisms: mean barrier remains sufficient after long-time spatial and collective dynamics
event-distribution and connectivity differences propagate into distinct long-time transport
collective correlations erase or reverse instantaneous rate differences
microstructural experimental factors dominate the mapping from bulk model to pellet conductivity

evidence.role: confirms initial-rate non-uniqueness but contains no long-time trajectory or conductivity target
contract-bound 30-pass paired-seed feasibility pilot showing finite execution but nonconverged, direction-unstable conductivity estimates
primary source for kMC conductivity, Haven ratio, correlation factor, vacancy, and experimental context

empirical_decision.rule: support only if a frozen mean-only model meets a preregistered conductivity equivalence bound across held-out configurations and matched-temperature experimental specimens
empirical_decision.evidence_summary: All six frozen 30-pass pilot runs complete with finite outputs, but the high-initial-rate/low-initial-rate conductivity ratio is 2.17, 3.16, and 0.106 across paired seeds, so the direction reverses. Thirty passes are only 1% of the source setting and do not close the long-time target.

closure_measurements: seeded convergence-checked kMC estimates of collective and tracer diffusion, Haven ratio, correlation factor, and conductivity
matched-temperature impedance data with pellet density, impurity, and grain-boundary controls

closure_experiments.measured_variable: long-time collective and tracer diffusivity, Haven ratio, correlation factor, simulated conductivity, and controlled experimental conductivity
closure_experiments.intervention_or_condition: use held-out same-composition configurations matched on the frozen mean-barrier rule but separated on event-distribution or connectivity strata; run paired random seeds to a frozen convergence criterion and compare against matched-temperature specimens

predictions.expected_outcome: matched-mean configurations and specimens remain inside the preregistered conductivity equivalence interval, and richer distribution/connectivity variables do not improve held-out prediction
predictions.rationale: a sufficient scalar coordinate should preserve long-time conductivity after composition and temperature matching

predictions.expected_outcome: matched-mean configurations retain systematic long-time transport differences explained by event multiplicity, low-barrier tails, connectivity, vacancies, or collective correlations
predictions.rationale: conductivity is generated by a nonlinear, spatially organized, correlated event process

predictions.expected_outcome: bulk kMC differences do not transfer consistently until pellet density, impurity phases, and grain-boundary impedance are controlled
predictions.rationale: experimental conductivity includes sample-level nuisance pathways absent from the bulk event model

closure_experiments.decision_rule: Promote mean-barrier sufficiency only if every held-out simulation stratum and experimental specimen block passes the frozen conductivity-equivalence criterion and no prespecified richer model improves held-out error beyond the equivalence margin.
closure_experiments.safety_or_ethics: standard solid-electrolyte computation, synthesis, and impedance controls
